_why: The files under `frontend/styles/components/` beside this manifest are
VERBATIM copies of CodeTracer's own Stylus component stylesheets. Together
they are the rules that DRAW a CodeTracer window: the tab strip and its
curved connectors, the panel surface and its splitters (golden_layout), the
buttons (button), the text inputs (input), the list rows (data_tables), the
'nothing here yet' treatment (empty_states) and the alert surfaces
(notifications).
THE LIVE PANES' SHEETS. Since Shared-DOM-Front-Ends Q6 the hydrated build
mounts CodeTracer's shared Call Trace, State and Event Log views, so their
sheets are here too (calltrace, state, event_log, list_scrubber), with the
right-click menu they open (menu_item, checkmark, and four rules of
text_editor, which is otherwise vendored for its mixin definitions only —
`StylSource.definitionsOnly` / `emitOnly`).
WHY BLOCKTRACER NEEDED THEM. The operator's report was that adopting
CodeTracer's TOKEN VALUES had not made the debugger look like CodeTracer —
'the way that tab bars look, panel separators, the elements inside the
panels'. It could not have: a token carries a colour, and the tab bar is a
RULE. BlockTracer tracks no .css/.scss/.styl file at all — every byte of its
CSS is a string literal in Nim — so none of CodeTracer's component CSS could
reach this markup, and `components/debugger_css.nim` had grown 2,500 lines
of BlockTracer's own hand-written pane chrome in its place. Two hand-written
chromes for one product is the divergence itself.
WHY A COPY AND NOT A BUILD DEPENDENCY. The alternative was to add Stylus to
this build and compile the real `.styl` files. Rejected on three measured
grounds, all of them recorded at length in `client/src/design_system/
ct_styl.nim`'s header: it puts node + the `stylus` package on the critical
path of a build whose own check scripts state they must run on a bare CI
runner with nothing but a shell and Nim; `codetracer.styl` resolves its
identifiers through `styles/generated/{brand,alias,mapped}.styl`, which are
generated from the SAME codetracer-design-system DTCG files that
`client/src/design_system/web.tokens.json` resolves against, so consuming
them raw would stand up a second, untracked token vocabulary beside `--bt-*`
and put every rule outside `tools/design/check-tokens.mjs`; and CodeTracer's
`.styl` has exactly one theme baked in while BlockTracer's debugger register
ships light AND dark.
SO THE RULES ARE PORTED, BUT MECHANICALLY. `design_system/ct_styl.nim` is a
Stylus-subset transpiler that compiles exactly these bytes;
`components/ct_components_css.nim` supplies the only three things
BlockTracer decides — an identifier bridge onto `--bt-*` roles, two
font-family aliases, and a listed set of rules that are dropped because the
markup they address cannot exist on a page with no JavaScript. Nobody
re-types a declaration, so the two products cannot drift by a hand slipping.
They can only drift by upstream moving, which is what part B below reports.
WHY THE DIRECTORY LOOKS LIKE CODETRACER'S. Same reason
`flow_layout.vendor.json` gives: this vendor root mirrors CodeTracer's
`src/`, so every copy stays byte-identical to upstream rather than needing
an edited path. `ct_components_css.nim` names each file by its UPSTREAM path
in the provenance comment it writes above that file's rules in the emitted
CSS, so a rule in the shipped stylesheet can be found upstream by reading
down from its header.
WHAT KEEPS THE COPY HONEST is `ci/test/ct-styles-vendor.sh`:
A. the bytes here still hash to the sha256s below (no local edits), and
the commit below EQUALS `ci/embed-sdk-pin.env`'s CODETRACER_REF, and
B. against a real CodeTracer checkout at that pin, each file is compared
byte for byte with its upstream path — so a change upstream fails here
with a diff to read, rather than leaving BlockTracer drawing a window
no other front-end draws.
Part B is a BYTE comparison here, unlike the two Nim manifests, which
compare by value because their files are allowed to differ in prose. These
are stylesheets: a reworded comment upstream changes what the transpiler
emits (comments are stripped, but a moved rule moves in the cascade), and
there is no 'observable' to compare short of the compiled CSS. A byte
comparison against the PIN — not against a moving checkout — is exact and
has no false positive.
NOTE ON THE COMMIT. It IS the Embed SDK pin, for the reason
`flow_layout.vendor.json` gives about its own: one commit, so the version
the handoff compiles against and the version the chrome is drawn from can
never be two different things. Moving the pin means re-vendoring every one
of these files in the same commit.
